extracted.intended_audience: educated London readers / general public interested in social conduct and manners
extracted.subtask_description: Short, periodical essays offering moral and social advice (courtship, family manners, country behaviour, avoidance of scandal) delivered in a satirical/instructive tone typical of The Spectator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtship by general agreeable conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The Way to this End I take to be, that a Man's general Conduct should be agreeable, without addressing in particular to the Woman he loves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice illustrated by the Damon/Strephon scheme: a successful suitor should cultivate an amiable, unconspicuous general manner (appear agreeable in company) rather than employ extravagant declarations. Examples: one man displays languishing rapture while the other appears indifferent; the indifferent man thereby wins the woman's eyes. Anti-pattern: ostentatious adoration that seems designed to procure pity rather than desire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be the object of desire, not of pity
rubrics_metrics.description: He that has her must be the Object of her Desire, not her Pity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking a woman's affection, a man's behaviour should inspire attraction rather than compassion. Overt shows of misery or entreaty (seeking pity) are ineffective; seeming disinterest and dignified conduct are more likely to produce genuine desire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appear disinterested to gain perceived sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: This seeming Unconcern gives this Behaviour the advantage of Sincerity, and insensibly obtains your good Opinion, by appearing disinterested in the purchase of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenting oneself as not actively vying for favour (disinterestedness) creates the appearance of sincerity and can strategically influence the beloved's opinion. Example: one man fatigues her with love-complaints while the other visits courteously afterward and reaps the benefit. Beware coordinated rivalry designed to manufacture this impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard and examine your heart before committing
rubrics_metrics.description: What I am concerned for, Madam, is, that in the disposal of your Heart, you should know what you are doing, and examine it before it is lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice to those being courted (especially women): scrutinize your feelings and motives before reciprocating, because manipulators may engineer reactions (alternating ardour and reserve) to secure attachment. Practical precaution: be on your guard and take necessary precautions against subtle, premeditated courtship tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring and preserve good-humour in country retirement
rubrics_metrics.description: take with them as great a Stock of Good-humour as they can; for tho' a Country-Life is described as the most pleasant of all others, and though it may in Truth be so, yet it is so only to those who know how to enjoy Leisure and Retirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before retiring from town to the country, ensure you can enjoy leisure without town amusements. Country life lacks the entertainments that relieve domestic repetition; therefore, preserving good-humour is essential to avoid mutual uneasiness among household and guests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Head of household's temper determines family atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: the Humour and Disposition of the Head, is what chiefly influences all the other Parts of a Family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The master or head's affability and benevolence set the tone for domestic relations; imitating Sir Roger's affability is recommended. To promote harmony, those in charge should display politeness and benevolence toward neighbours and servants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforce group rules (an 'Infirmary') to preserve ease
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a large Wing of the House which they design to employ in the Nature of an Infirmary. Whoever says a peevish thing, or acts any thing which betrays a Sowerness or Indisposition to Company, is immediately to be conveyed to his Chambers in the Infirmary...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical institutional rule for clubs/households: temporarily exclude (banish to 'infirmary') anyone who displays ill-natured words or gestures, impatience with servants, making others repeat themselves, or general inattention/dishumour. Relief is conditional on a humble petition and observable submission; this both protects the group's ease and incentivises good conduct. Self-removal when one senses ill-humour is specifically rewarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward self-awareness and voluntary retreat from ill-humour
rubrics_metrics.description: whoever observes the ill-natured Fit coming upon himself, and voluntarily retires, shall be received at his return from the Infirmary with the highest Marks of Esteem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage members to withdraw voluntarily when they feel peevish; reintegration should be met with esteem. This promotes restraint and accountability rather than permanent ostracism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid and distrust anonymous or flimsy scandal
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many who are known to have ill-will ... There are many who are naturally addicted to Defamation... _I shall not desire, that if any Report to our Disadvantage has any Ground for it, you would overlook or extenuate it: But if there be any thing advanced without a Person who can say whence he had it ... all such Testimonies as these ... you will think too slight to have any Credit against the Innocence and Honour of your Fellow-Citizen_.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating rumours or scandalous reports, require attribution and reliable attestation. Reports without a named source or based on hearsay should be treated as too slight to impugn someone's honour. Use skepticism: scandal spreads swiftly and is easily believed, but lacks credibility without traceable source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize typical traits of scandal-bearers (gossip sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lazy, the Idle, and the Froward, are the Persons who are most pleas'd with the little Tales which pass about the Town to the Disadvantage of the rest of the World... The Unwillingness to receive good Tidings is a Quality as inseparable from a Scandal-Bearer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that certain characters (idle, peevish, malicious, or confined persons like the Lady Bluemantle) are prone to inventing or repeating gossip: they may not know original authorship and often transmit tales without verification. Treat their reports skeptically and avoid feeding such malice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for kind correspondence and avoid feuds in families
rubrics_metrics.description: An Agreement and kind Correspondence between Friends and Acquaintance, is the greatest Pleasure of Life... we commonly meet with ill-natured Expostulations, Noise, and Chidings...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote concord: mutual forbearance and civility among family and acquaintances maximizes domestic pleasure. Given the tendency for small irritations to escalate in confined company (e.g., in country stays), one should practise patience and actively avoid provoking jealousies and quarrels.
